statement: Jennifer Nez Denetdale, "Chairmen, Presidents, and Princesses: The Navajo Nation, Gender, and the Politics of Tradition," Wicazo Sa Review 21(1) (2006): 9-28 [CRITICAL INDIGENOUS/FEMINIST], argues the current Navajo Nation government's patriarchal exclusion of women from its highest offices (no woman has ever been elected Navajo Nation Council Chair or President; women were not extended the vote in Navajo Nation elections until 1928) is a specifically colonial/settler imposition — the US-imposed 1923 tribal-council model, created originally to certify oil and gas leases — laid over, and actively distorting, an indigenous kinship-based system of authority that traditional ethnography (Kluckhohn and Leighton, 1946/1974) documents as matrilineal/matrilocal with real, if informal, female decision-making authority.

sources.citation: Denetdale, Jennifer Nez. "Chairmen, Presidents, and Princesses: The Navajo Nation, Gender, and the Politics of Tradition." Wicazo Sa Review 21(1), 2006: 9-28.
